title: Regional quantized burstbuffer sizer (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working calculator + rationale for sizing a regional GPU pool that accounts for: quantized model variants (4-bit/8-bit), burst buffering (short-duration spike capacity), and region-local KV cache footprint. Use case: private/VPC deployments where customers need predictable latency SLOs but can accept degraded throughput during microbursts.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Goal: produce a conservative BOM and scaling guidance for a medium-size enterprise private deployment (3 regions) supporting low-latency chat and batch embedding workloads.
- Primary levers: model quantization profile, per-request token distribution, steady-state QPS vs burst QPS, prefix/KV cache hit rate, batch window.
- Deliverables here: rough node SKU list, headroom multiplier, NVMe burst buffer sizing, and worked example scenarios.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Models: 2 variants: LLM-chat (base fp16 ~70B) quantized to 8-bit or 4-bit runtime variants. Embedding model is smaller (2B FP16) - quantized to 8-bit.
- Effective per-GPU capacity: baseline numbers are empirical from lab runs (see linked runbook):
  * 8-bit chat: 120 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent (single-tenant conservative)
  * 4-bit chat: 220 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent (improved throughput due to 4-bit kernels)
  * embedding model: 400 qps per GPU (small mem, high throughput)
- Typical request profile (p50/p90 token lengths): 32/128 tokens for chat; embedding size fixed.
- Cache: prefix/KV caching reduces average token compute by 18% at 60% cache hit rate.
- Burst profile: steady-state QPS = 400 chat requests/min (global per region), burst peak = 4x steady-state for short windows (1-5 minutes) for traffic spikes.
- SLO: p95 generation latency target: < 300ms for chat response streaming (this drives headroom).
- Node SKUs considered: 1) 2x A100-80GB (dense 2-GPU NVLink node), 2) 4x H100-80GB equivalent (if available), 3) 1x A10x or L4 (edge-style) for embeddings.

Methodology / calculator steps (manual form):
1) Convert request QPS -> tokens/sec demand: tokens/sec_demand = QPS * tokens_per_request.
2) Adjust for cache effect: effective_tokens/sec = tokens/sec_demand * (1 - cache_hit_rate * avg_prefix_reduction).
3) Select quantization throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) based on model variant.
4) Base GPUs required = ceil(effective_tokens/sec / tokens/sec_per_gpu).
5) Apply batch efficiency multiplier (e.g., 0.9 for small batches) and reserve headroom (1.3x for p95 SLO).
6) Add burst buffer capacity: determine extra GPU-equivalents needed for short bursts and backstop with NVMe burst nodes to absorb queueing without violating SLOs.
7) Map GPU-equivalents to nodes based on SKU choices and calculate NVMe/DRAM/CPU per node.

Worked example (3-region deployment)
Inputs:
- regions: us-west, us-east, eu-west (traffic split 40/40/20)
- steady-state chat QPS (global): 1,200 req/min -> per-region steady QPS: 480/480/240 req/min -> convert to QPS (req/sec): 8/8/4
- avg tokens/request: p50=32, but use p90=128 for conservative sizing -> tokens/request = 128
- cache_hit_rate = 0.6, avg_prefix_reduction = 0.25 (cache saves 25% of tokens when hit)
- quantization: choose mixed strategy: us-west and eu-west use 4-bit for chat, us-east uses 8-bit (customer preference / hardware availability)
- burst multiplier: 4x for 3-minute windows

Calculations (per-region, show us-west):
1) tokens/sec_demand = QPS * tokens_per_request = 8 * 128 = 1,024 tokens/sec
2) effective_tokens/sec = 1,024 * (1 - 0.6 * 0.25) = 1,024 * (1 - 0.15) = 870 tokens/sec
3) tokens/sec_per_gpu (4-bit chat) = 220 tokens/sec per GPU -> base_gpus = ceil(870 / 220) = ceil(3.95) = 4 GPUs
4) apply batch efficiency 0.9 -> adjusted_base = 4 / 0.9 = 4.44 -> round up to 5 GPUs
5) apply headroom 1.3x (p95 SLO) -> production_gpus = ceil(5 * 1.3) = ceil(6.5) = 7 GPUs
6) burst capacity: burst_tokens/sec = 4 * 870 = 3,480 tokens/sec -> GPUs_needed_at_burst = ceil(3,480 / 220) = ceil(15.8) = 16 GPUs.
7) transient oversubscription strategy: keep production_gpus=7, provide a burst buffer (NVMe-backed queue + 9 spare GPUs in the region) OR rely on cross-region fallback (but cross-region adds latency). Prefer local spare capacity: spare_gpus_for_burst = 16 - 7 = 9 GPUs.

Node mapping (SKU choice = 2x A100-80GB per node):
- GPUs per node = 2 -> us-west production nodes = ceil(7 / 2) = 4 nodes (8 GPUs)
- spare for burst = 9 GPUs -> 5 nodes spare = 10 GPUs (rounded up)
- total nodes in region = 9 nodes (18 GPUs) -> spare capacity ratio = (18 - 8) / 8 = 125% spare over base prod GPUs (pretty conservative).

NVMe burst buffer sizing (rationale and calc):
- Burst buffer purpose: short-lived queueing so requests are not dropped and to smooth loading during short spikes while spare GPUs come up or batches are formed.
- Estimate average request working set (tokens->KV & prefix footprint): assume 1.5MB per chat request live memory footprint (KV pointers + small context). For 4-minute worst-case backlog at burst: backlog_requests = burst_QPS_seconds * 240s. For us-west: burst_QPS_seconds = burst_tokens/sec / tokens_per_request = 3,480 / 128 ≈ 27.19 req/sec -> backlog ~ 27.19 * 240 ≈ 6,525 requests.
- NVMe storage for backlog = 6,525 * 1.5MB ≈ 9.8GB (round to 32GB to allow overhead + index).
- But we need read/write throughput: each backlog request may be paged to/from NVMe once; plan NVMe IOPS and bandwidth accordingly. Choose 4 x 2TB NVMe per node (to support concurrency and provide local scratch).

Cost roughing (estimates, not final procurement):
- 2x A100-80GB node list price (placeholder): $45k/node (TCO depends on OPEX / support).
- us-west nodes: 9 -> hardware list ~ $405k (capex).
- add networking (200Gbps switches, cross-region egress buffer) ~ $40k one-time + operational egress costs.
- NVMe + DRAM + CPU: included in node price estimate but call out 4x NVMe per node, 1.5TB DRAM target for large KV caches.

Operational notes & heuristics (bulleted):
- Prefer spare GPU capacity localized per region for latency-sensitive paths; cross-region fallback only for non-interactive features or when region costs are prohibitive.
- Use quantization mix to trade cost/throughput: 4-bit for chat where quality regression is acceptable; keep 8-bit for conservative customers or where hybrid precision inference is required.
- For embedding-heavy customers, consider deploying separate CPU/cheap-GPU cluster (A10x/L4) to keep expensive high-memory GPUs for chat.
- Autoscaler behavior: maintain production_gpus as steady baseline; keep a warm pool of spare nodes that can be quickly powered (or use preemptible with rapid warm fallback).

Open questions / TODOs (remaining action items):
- Verify empirical tokens/sec per GPU for our 4-bit kernels with long-context (2k+) prompts—lab tests scheduled (Runbook ID in linked_artifacts).
- Model quality check for mixed quantization at per-region granularity; run A/B on p95 latency vs hallucination rate.
- Confirm procurement budget authority for >40 nodes across regions; finance sign-off needed.
- Decide whether NVMe burst buffer is per-node or per-cluster; per-cluster might be more cost-effective but adds cross-node traffic.

Appendix: quick calc snippets (copy into sheet):
- tokens/sec_demand = (QPS_per_region) * (tokens_per_request)
- effective_tokens = tokens/sec_demand * (1 - cache_hit_rate * avg_prefix_reduction)
- base_gpus = ceil(effective_tokens / throughput_per_gpu)
- adjusted_gpus = ceil(base_gpus / batch_efficiency)
- production_gpus = ceil(adjusted_gpus * headroom_multiplier)
- burst_gpus = ceil((burst_multiplier * effective_tokens) / throughput_per_gpu)

Notes to self: keep this doc short-form; the canonical spreadsheet will live in the private-deployments sizer workbook. This file documents the burst-buffer focused methodology we can reuse across customers. If we move to autoscaling with faster spin-up (30s), the spare ratios above can be reduced substantially.

End of working notes.
